summary: US-B2b: The role matrix — box office cannot touch settlement
description:
**As** the platform owner, **I want** every staff-reachable route classified by role and enforced server-side, **so that** box-office staff cannot reach finance or settlement surfaces even if they guess the URL.

Slice (b) of the former TKT-191, split on the owner's decision (2026-08-03). Slice (a) — closing the unauthenticated catalog write surface — is **TKT-191**, which this is blocked by. TKT-190 proved *who*; TKT-191 shut the back door; this proves *what they may do*.

**Where enforcement goes.** Into TKT-190's composed gate (`gateRequest`, `web/backoffice/src/lib/gate.ts`) — the one place a session and a route are both in hand, and the function that already owns the only calls to `next` and `lookup` so the ordering is testable. Do not add a second enforcement point.

**In scope:** the role enum (`admin`, `box_office`, `finance`); the route→role matrix as a single declared table; enforcement in the composed gate; a fail-closed test over the real route table; role-aware nav (defense in depth, never the enforcement); the role travelling from the staff account into the session (TKT-190 stores the column and returns nothing).

**Out of scope:** per-object permissions, per-organizer scoping, a role administration UI, delegation/impersonation, and re-opening where the catalog write credential lives (TKT-191 settled it).

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] Every staff-reachable route is classified in **one** declared matrix, and a test enumerates the real route table and **fails** if any route is reachable with no classification.
- [ ] A `finance` session is refused on the **catalog authoring surface** (`/admin/venues/*` — the
      seat-map authoring pages that exist today); an `admin` session reaches every staff-reachable
      route. Each proven by driving the real route, not by asserting on the matrix table.
- [ ] **The finance/settlement surface does not exist yet** (TKT-23 owns it), so "box office cannot
      touch settlement" cannot be driven end to end here. Instead: the matrix must be able to
      express a route no role but `finance` may reach, and a test must prove that classification is
      enforced — using a route that exists. Do **not** invent a settlement page to test against, and
      do **not** quietly drop the requirement; state in the ticket which half is proven now and
      which lands with TKT-23.
- [ ] The refusal discloses neither the required role nor whether the route exists.
- [ ] The nav renders only in-role links, **and** a direct request to a hidden URL is still refused — proving the nav is not the enforcement.
- [ ] The role reaches the session from the staff account, and a role that is not in the enum fails closed rather than being treated as permissive.
- [ ] Anonymous callers are still refused before any role check runs; TKT-190's tests pass untouched.
- [ ] Verified by a browser: sign in as each role and confirm what renders and what is refused.

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS + gateway smoke suite).
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary; OpenAPI regenerated and committed before the gate (ADR-009).
- UI story: the write forms are **submitted** against the real stack (`make up`), not just rendered.
- Read endpoints declare their ADR-004 TTL tier; auth/session responses are `no-store`.

governingAdrs.why: The gateway is the single public entry point and its route table IS the security boundary. Anything added to the edge must keep that construction true.
Contract-first: a new HTTP surface is authored in openapi.yaml and the generated code committed BEFORE the gate — check-generate diffs against HEAD.
Response drift fails closed: a 401/403 the handler can emit must be declared, or the validator turns it into a 500.
The back office is Astro SSR behind the gateway; checkOrigin is off and form actions must be RELATIVE.

Records where staff identity and sessions live, why the back office does not hold INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN, and — in its adversary section — names the unauthenticated catalog write surface as the gap these two tickets close.

Name the adversary before claiming a guarantee. Neither ticket produces tamper-evidence; both constrain a caller arriving through the gateway and neither constrains anyone with network access to a container or write access to the database.

Amended by TKT-191. Catalog now authenticates the back office as a DEPUTY holding a write-capable credential — which is exactly why this ticket matters: the deputy's rule for who may drive which write is currently 'any signed-in staff member', and the role matrix is what replaces it.

reference.summary: SHARED CREDENTIAL BLAST RADIUS (decomposition.md § context-mémo): INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN is ONE value across all five services (compose.yaml, the &go-env anchor). It opens commerce /internal/orders/{id}/refunds, inventory /internal/operational-holds and /internal/slots/{id}/capacity-adjustments, and access's refund surface. It must NOT be the credential these tickets give the back office.
TKT-190's composed gate — where the matrix attaches, and the function that owns the only calls to next/lookup so ordering stays testable.
The staff_accounts.role column: stored by TKT-190, returned by nothing, enforced nowhere.
TKT-191's credential means the browser never holds a catalog credential, so the back-office route matrix IS the enforcement point for catalog writes — there is no second path to guard.

# TKT-197 execution plan — role matrix

## Design decision

Add one route-policy module, `web/backoffice/src/lib/authorization.ts` **(NEW)**. It will contain the single declared `ROUTE_MATRIX` **(NEW)** read by both `gateRequest` and the navigation renderer.

| Route template | Classification | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| `/admin/` | authenticated page | `admin`, `box_office`, `finance` |
| `/admin/venues/[id]` | authenticated, role-exclusive authoring page | `admin` only |
| `/admin/logout` | authenticated endpoint | `admin`, `box_office`, `finance` |
| `/admin/login` | anonymous page | all callers |
| `/admin/healthz` | anonymous endpoint | all callers |
| `/admin/_astro/[...asset]` **(NEW synthetic entry)** | anonymous build asset | all callers |

This makes the existing venue-authoring route the proof that the matrix can express and enforce an exclusive route: only `admin` may reach it. When TKT-23 adds settlement, it must add its page to this same matrix as `admin` + `finance`, hide its navigation from `box_office`, and add the missing real-route/direct-write proof. TKT-197 will not invent a settlement route.

One correction to the brief’s HEAD inventory: `/admin/logout` is not anonymous today. `isAnonymousPath` exempts login, health, and `_astro/*`; existing tests explicitly pin that set. Logout should remain authenticated so an anonymous request is refused before its handler runs.

## 1. Fail-closed route enumeration

`web/backoffice/test/authorization.test.ts` **(NEW)** will recursively walk the real `web/backoffice/src/pages/` directory with Node’s standard `fs`/`path` APIs and derive Astro templates:

- Strip supported page/endpoint extensions.
- Collapse `index.astro` to the containing route.
- Preserve `[id]` as a one-segment dynamic template.
- Include `.ts` API endpoints, so `logout.ts` and `healthz.ts` are covered.
- Compare the derived set with all `source: 'page'` entries in `ROUTE_MATRIX` **(NEW)** in both directions.

The equality check prevents both failure shapes:

- A new page without a matrix row fails the build.
- A stale matrix row with no page also fails, avoiding another silently miscounted hand-maintained list.

The matcher used at runtime will compile the same templates: `[id]` matches exactly one segment; `[...asset]` matches the asset suffix; trailing-slash normalization remains explicit. Unsupported route syntax under `pages/` will fail the test rather than be ignored.

What this proof cannot see:

- It sees the dynamic route definition, not every concrete `[id]` value.
- It sees an API route’s path, not which HTTP method exports the file implements; authorization remains path-level and runs before Astro’s method dispatch.
- It cannot see a custom route injected from `astro.config.mjs`, an integration, or middleware. There is no such custom routing at HEAD; adding one must extend the enumerator or be prohibited.
- A component outside `src/pages/` is not a route in the current Astro configuration. If later mounted by custom routing, the filesystem test alone will not find it.
- Built `_astro` assets are generated rather than page files, hence the explicit synthetic matrix row.

As a mutation check, temporarily add `web/backoffice/src/pages/__coverage_probe.astro` **(NEW, temporary, never committed)**, confirm the enumeration test fails for the missing classification, then remove it.

## 2. Role vocabulary and invalid stored roles

The authoritative vocabulary will be `components/schemas/StaffRole` **(NEW)** in `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml`:

```text
admin | box_office | finance
```

`StaffPrincipal.role` **(NEW)** will be required and reference that enum. Under ADR-009, this is the single source; `make generate` derives:

- Go `StaffRole` and its constants **(NEW)**.
- TypeScript `components['schemas']['StaffRole']` **(NEW)** in both generated clients.

The TypeScript permission objects will be exhaustively typed against the generated union, so adding a contract role without deciding every route permission fails compilation.

No new migration and no vocabulary `CHECK` will be added. `staff_accounts.role` remains non-empty text because:

- A SQL enum/check would create a second handwritten vocabulary.
- It does not provide browser authorization.
- It does not constrain a database writer, who can also change the constraint or assign `admin`.
- Legacy or out-of-band values still require a fail-closed application boundary.

Instead, an unknown stored role will be rejected before a successful principal response. `AuthenticateStaff` will validate the store value against generated `StaffRole` constants and return its already-declared generic 500 without echoing the value. `authenticateStaff()` will also reject a response whose role is not recognized, and `gateRequest` will deny an unknown role if one nevertheless reaches a session. Thus no unknown value becomes permissive.

Migration `0015` receives comment-only stale-reference cleanup; its schema remains unchanged.

## 3. Role propagation

The propagation chain will be:

```text
staff_accounts.role
  → store.StaffAccount.Role
  → OpenAPI StaffPrincipal.role
  → authenticateStaff() camel-case DTO
  → session.StaffPrincipal.role
  → App.Locals.staff.role
  → gateRequest / navigation
```

Changes:

- Add `StaffRole` **(NEW)** and required `role` to `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml`.
- Update `services/catalog/internal/api/staff.go` to return the validated role.
- Run `make generate`.
- Commit `services/catalog/internal/api/openapi_gen.go`, both generated `api-types.gen.ts` files, and the schema change before `make check`.
- Update `web/backoffice/src/lib/api.ts` to map `body.role`.
- Extend `web/backoffice/src/lib/session.ts`’s existing `StaffPrincipal`.
- `web/backoffice/src/env.d.ts` needs no structural edit because `App.Locals.staff` already references that interface.

`scripts/smoke.sh` currently provisions one `admin`. Add distinct `finance` and `box_office` accounts and pass their generated credentials to the smoke process.

Role is snapshotted at sign-in. Because there is no supported role-change operation today, this is acceptable, but ADR-042 must state that a future role-change surface must invalidate or refresh existing sessions; otherwise an old role survives until logout, restart, eviction, or the eight-hour expiry.

## 4. Enforcement inside `gateRequest`

Preserve this exact order:

1. Refuse an unsafe untrusted-origin request.
2. Determine whether the route is explicitly anonymous.
3. For every other path—including an unclassified path—perform session lookup.
4. If no session resolves, redirect to login immediately.
5. Classify the path and evaluate the resolved principal’s role.
6. On missing classification, unknown role, or denied role, return the existing generic `forbiddenResponse`.
7. Only then call `onAuthenticated` and `next`.

This preserves COS-7: an anonymous request fails at authentication before any role evaluation. The existing TKT-190 anonymous redirect test remains untouched and distinguishes the ordering: moving authorization first would produce 403 rather than its pinned 302.

`gateRequest` remains the only owner of `lookup` and `next`; `middleware.ts` stays a pure adapter.

## 5. Test seams by condition of success

- **COS-1 — enumeration:** `authorization.test.ts` **(NEW)** walks the real page tree and compares it exactly with the matrix’s page entries.
- **COS-2 — finance refused/admin universal:** smoke-sign in as both roles; drive `/admin/venues/00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1`; expect finance 403 and admin 200.
- **COS-3 — exclusive-route capability:** the same real venue route is `admin`-exclusive. TKT-23 owns adding and driving the future finance/settlement route, including the box-office refusal.
- **COS-4 — no disclosure:** with one authenticated denied session, compare the response from the real venue route with `/admin/definitely-not-a-page`; both must be the same generic 403 and name neither role nor route.
- **COS-5 — nav is not enforcement:** finance and box-office venue-list HTML must contain no `Author seat maps` link or `/admin/venues/` target. Then manually request the known hidden URL with the same session and still receive 403. The second assertion is what proves navigation is not the control.
- **COS-6 — propagation/unknown role:** catalog handler, API client, and session tests pin role propagation. A fake stored unsupported role produces no successful principal/session; a forged unsupported session is denied by the gate.
- **COS-7 — authentication ordering:** retain all TKT-190 assertions unchanged; add role tests around them rather than weakening or rewriting their fixtures.

The existing authoring links in `web/backoffice/src/pages/index.astro` are the relevant navigation surface at HEAD. They will call `canAccessRoute` **(NEW)** from the same policy module used by the gate.

## 6. TDD order

1. **Contract red**

   Change `TestAuthenticateStaffReturnsThePrincipal` to require `role: admin`; it currently fails because the response omits it. Add an unsupported stored-role case expecting generic 500; current behavior returns 200.

2. **Client/session red**

   Add API mapping and typed-session assertions requiring the role to round-trip. Before implementation the field is absent. Add an unknown-response-role test expecting rejection; current code accepts and discards it.

3. **Enumeration red**

   Add the filesystem equality test against `ROUTE_MATRIX` **(NEW)**. Before the policy exists it fails to compile; with an empty scaffold it reports all five page templates as unclassified. Perform the temporary-page mutation check.

4. **Gate red**

   Add tests where `finance` and `box_office` request a venue route: expect 403 and `next === 0`; today both reach downstream. Add admin success, unknown-role refusal, and unclassified-path refusal. Compare real/unknown refusal bodies.

5. **Navigation and real-stack red**

   Provision all three roles. Before filtering/enforcement, finance and box-office HTML contains authoring links and their direct requests return 200; both assertions must turn green. Admin must retain the links and reach the page.

6. **Documentation and stale wording**

   Amend ADR-042 and update operational documentation only after the executable behavior is green.

## 7. Files

### Contract and catalog

- `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` — add `StaffRole` **(NEW)**, carry required `role`, and correct superseded public/TKT-191 wording.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` — regenerated Go contract.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/staff.go` — validate and return the stored role; correct stale deputy comments.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/staff_test.go` — reverse the obsolete “principal must not carry role” assertion and cover unknown-role failure.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/staff.go` — correct the stale TKT-191 ownership comment.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/staff_smoke_test.go` — update stale “nothing enforces it yet” wording.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0015_staff_accounts.sql` — comment-only ownership correction; no schema change.
- `services/catalog/cmd/catalog/provision_staff.go` — correct stale flag/help text without introducing a second vocabulary.

### Back office

- `web/backoffice/src/lib/authorization.ts` **(NEW)** — declared matrix, template matcher, recognized-role and access helpers.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/gate.ts` — attach role enforcement after session lookup and fail closed for unclassified routes.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/api.ts` — map and validate the returned role.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/session.ts` — retain role in the opaque server-side session principal.
- `web/backoffice/src/pages/index.astro` — render authoring links only when the matrix allows them.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts` — regenerated TypeScript contract.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts` — regenerated because the shared catalog contract generates both clients.
- `web/backoffice/test/authorization.test.ts` **(NEW)** — real-directory enumeration and matcher/policy tests.
- `web/backoffice/test/gate.test.ts` — append role enforcement/refusal tests; leave existing TKT-190 cases untouched.
- `web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts` — role mapping and unknown-role refusal.
- `web/backoffice/test/session.test.ts` — typed role round-trip.

### Integration and documentation

- `scripts/smoke.sh` — provision `admin`, `finance`, and `box_office`.
- `smoke/backoffice_venue_list_test.go` — real sign-ins, filtered links, direct hidden-URL refusal, admin reachability, and non-disclosing 403 comparison.
- `docs/adr/ADR-042-staff-identity-and-backoffice-sessions.md` — add the TKT-197 amendment, replace “any signed-in staff member,” record session snapshot semantics and the adversary boundary.
- `docs/development.md` — document vocabulary, matrix behavior, provisioning, and TKT-23’s remaining settlement half.

Explicitly unchanged:

- `compose.yaml` — no new service, environment variable, or deployment wiring.
- No new migration file or database constraint.
- `.github/workflows/check.yaml` and `Makefile` — CI continues to invoke the mirrored `make check`.
- Gateway and catalog write-credential enforcement.
- Dependencies and lockfiles.

## 8. Definition of done

- All five page/endpoint files and the generated asset prefix have exactly one classification.
- A temporary unclassified page makes the enumeration test fail.
- `admin` reaches every declared staff route; `finance` and `box_office` receive generic 403 on venue authoring.
- Restricted navigation is absent, while a pasted hidden URL remains refused.
- Unknown stored/response/session roles cannot reach downstream.
- Existing anonymous, origin-ordering, sign-out, replay, and cache tests pass unchanged.
- ADR-042 names the constrained adversary: a signed-in staff member driving the browser. Anyone holding `CATALOG_STAFF_WRITE_TOKEN`, controlling the back-office process, or writing the database remains outside the guarantee.
- In a real browser against `make up`, submit admin and restricted-role login forms; as admin submit an existing venue authoring form, and as finance/box-office paste the hidden authoring URL and observe the generic refusal.
- Run `make generate` and commit generated outputs before the gate.
- Run `make check` as the sole command in its shell invocation. Judge success from the full log body and explicitly inspect for `Error [0-9]+`, `FAIL`, or `drifted`, not only the reported exit code.

## Risks and estimate

The highest-risk defect is disagreement between filesystem-derived templates and the runtime matcher—especially `index`, trailing slashes, `[id]`, and `.ts` endpoints. The cheapest early check is the focused enumeration suite plus the temporary unclassified-page mutation before touching smoke tests.

Other review risks are role snapshot lifetime, accidentally treating unknown roles as “all staff,” and filtering links without gating direct requests. Each has an independent test above.

Estimated size: **medium, approximately 350–400 changed lines including tests, documentation, and generated diffs**, with no new dependency, service, migration behavior, money path, or gateway change.

No files were modified while drafting this plan.

### Plan-final — TKT-197

**The `kind=plan` draft as amended below is the plan.** Delta, not a restatement.

Critique by **main-agent** (`config.models.planReview`); draft by `gpt-5.6-sol`. Cross-model pair holds.

---

#### 1. Seam and mechanism verification at HEAD (`f29d7e02`)

| Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `gateRequest` owns the only calls to `next` and `lookup`; `middleware.ts` is a pure adapter | ✅ |
| A named enum schema generates Go constants via oapi-codegen | ✅ — `openapi_gen.go` already carries `// Defines values for ClosureStatus`, `FestivalStatus`, `PerformanceStatus`, `PriceResolutionFallbackReason`, and access has four more. The `StaffRole` mechanism is proven in-repo, not hoped for. |
| `staff_accounts.role` is non-empty text with **no vocabulary CHECK** (migration `0015`) | ✅ |
| `StaffPrincipal` carries only `staff_id` / `organizer_id`; `staff.go` builds it from those two | ✅ |
| Stale "TKT-191 owns role semantics" pointers in the schema, `store/staff.go`, and a test asserting the principal has no role | ✅ all three exist |
| Route surface is 5 files under `src/pages/` | ✅ |
| `web/backoffice/src/env.d.ts` needs no structural edit (it references the interface) | ✅ |

#### 2. The draft corrected the brief — recorded, because it matters

**My brief stated that `logout.ts` is anonymous. It is not.** `isAnonymousPath` returns true for
exactly `LOGIN_PATH`, `HEALTHZ_PATH` and the `_astro/` prefix (`gate.ts:30`); `LOGOUT_PATH` is
defined but never exempted, so sign-out is an authenticated endpoint today.

The draft caught it, said so plainly, and drew the right conclusion — logout **stays** authenticated,
so an anonymous request is refused before its handler runs.

This is the drafter falsifying the critic, which is the direction this pipeline usually does not
run, and it is worth naming: I supplied that "verified fact" in a section headed *"Verified facts at
HEAD — do not re-derive"*. It was not verified. A drafter that had trusted the brief would have
opened a hole in the exemption list, and the exemption list **is** the anonymous attack surface.

#### 3. Cons read against the Decision

Nothing self-refuting. The draft's own limits section is unusually honest — it enumerates what the
filesystem enumeration *cannot* see (dynamic values vs. definitions, HTTP methods, config-injected
routes, components outside `pages/`) rather than claiming the derivation is total. That is the right
shape for a fail-closed claim, and it is what makes COS-1 assessable.

#### 4. Amendments

**A1 — accepted, and it is the best idea in the draft.** Enumeration compares the filesystem and the
matrix **in both directions**: a new page without a row fails, *and* a stale row with no page fails.
One-way would have left the matrix able to accumulate rows for routes that no longer exist —
harmless-looking, and exactly how a matrix stops describing reality. Adopted as specified.

**A2 — accepted, promoted to mandatory.** The draft proposes a **mutation check**: add a temporary
unclassified page, confirm the enumeration test fails, remove it. That is the "verify the test can
fail" discipline this run has needed on every ticket — three times on TKT-191, where a test that
could not fail survived a full review pass. **It is not optional and its result is reported in the
coding summary**, not merely performed.

**A3 — amended. `provision-staff` must validate the role against the generated constants.**
The draft leaves the CLI accepting any non-empty string and relies on sign-in failing later. That is
fail-closed but hostile: an operator who types `--role adminn` gets a successful provision, a
created account, and then a **generic 500** at first sign-in with nothing pointing at the typo.

Validate in the CLI against the same generated `StaffRole` constants — **not** a second vocabulary,
which is the thing the draft is right to avoid. One source, checked at the point where a human can
still fix it cheaply. The error names the accepted values; it is an operator-facing message, not a
response to an untrusted caller.

**A4 — amended, wording. The unknown-stored-role 500 needs a comment saying why it is a 500.**
The draft is right to choose 500 over 401: an unrecognised stored role is a data problem, and
answering "invalid credentials" would send an operator to reset a password that was never wrong.
But a bare 500 on the sign-in path is indistinguishable from an outage, so the *code* must say what
it means, and `docs/development.md` must tell an operator that a sudden 500 for one account with
everyone else working means that account's role is not in the vocabulary.

**A5 — accepted, and the ADR must carry it. Role is snapshotted at sign-in.**
The draft spotted that a role change would not reach a live session for up to eight hours. There is
no role-change surface today, so this is correct-and-bounded rather than a defect — but it is
exactly the kind of fact that is obvious now and invisible in six months. ADR-042's amendment states
it, and states that a future role-change surface must invalidate or refresh sessions.

**A6 — accepted with a size warning, no change.** ~350–400 estimated against a **22-file** manifest.
The last two tickets estimated 950–1,150 → ~3,000, and 360–400 → ~1,100. Expect ~700–900. Not a
reason to re-plan; a reason to stop and say what grew if it exceeds that, rather than pushing an
unreadable diff. Nothing on the draft's list may be cut to make the number.

**A7 — accepted, flagged for the reviewer.** With `/admin/venues/[id]` as `admin`-only, `box_office`
can currently reach **only** the venue list. That looks wrong and is not: the surfaces box office
will actually use are the order console (TKT-193) and its actions (TKT-194). Say so in the matrix's
comment, so the next reader does not "fix" it by widening the classification.

Draft carried its own risk list. Critic applied **inversion** — *what guarantees this ticket fails?*

### learnings:

1. **Mirror a router's precedence by reading it, not by describing it.** Authorization that maps a
   URL to a rule must agree with the router about which route that URL *is*; two hand-reasoned
   approximations of Astro's `routeComparator` each left a role-inverting hole, and reading
   `priority.js` fixed it in one pass. → **`docs/learnings/`**, and it generalizes to any framework
   whose routing table an authorization layer shadows.

2. **A derived, fail-closed enumeration does not protect the step that *selects* among matches.**
   TKT-197's route enumeration is bidirectional and mutation-verified, and the [high] defect sat in
   rule selection — invisible to it, because both templates existed in both sets. Deriving the *set*
   is not deriving the *decision*. → **`docs/learnings/`**.

3. **A guard written around one example is a guard around one example.** `[` at index 0 rejected
   `order-[id]` and accepted `[id]-edit`. The fix is to state the property positively (what IS
   supported) rather than enumerate what is not. → covered by 2; **no separate promotion**.

4. **`vitest` does not typecheck.** Twice this run, fixtures missing a newly required field ran green
   and failed at `tsc` in the gate. Running the TS build locally before the gate turns a ~3-minute
   compose cycle into a two-second one. → **retro item, below**.

### retro:

**(1) What would have made this ticket faster or better?**

- **Run the TypeScript build before invoking the gate.** Two of six gate runs on this ticket failed
  on `tsc` errors that `pnpm vitest` cannot see, each costing a full compose cycle. **Concrete
  change: `SKILL.md` § Building — before running `config.code.localGate`, run the project's
  fastest type/lint check if it has one separate from the gate.** Cheap, and it is the same class as
  the existing "commit generated files before the gate" rule.

- **The plan's own mutation check found nothing; the review found five things.** The drafter proposed
  the mutation check and I promoted it to mandatory — it did confirm the enumeration works, which was
  worth having. But the defects were all in *selection* and *shape*, which no amount of mutating the
  enumeration would surface. **No process change proposed:** this is the honest limit of a
  self-designed check, and it is exactly why the cross-model review exists.

**(2) What should the humans change?**

- **The fix-diff pattern is now measured, across three tickets.** TKT-190: 6 of 9 findings in fix
